scope: the cols encoder's hint2 trailer layout, and what it implies for our surplus

structure: a FIXED list of eight hint fields in table order: 82, 89, 93, 98, 101, 104, 106, 122
each entry writes ONE gate bit (value != 0), and only when the width is non-zero AND the value is non-zero does it write the payload
the first entry (82, the radar codec) instead writes one gate bit and, when present, six more bits
the loop BREAKS as soon as `index >= last_changed`, so the trailer is gated by the same `last` value that gates the field loop

what_this_implies: with `last_changed = 0` (what our bodies write) the trailer writes NOTHING - every hint index is >= 0
so the trailer does not explain the 14-16 bit surplus we measured with last=0
but it does explain why a REAL server's ps is much longer: its `last_changed` is large, so the trailer engages
and it means our `last` value is doing double duty: it gates the field loop AND the hint trailer
the_next_experiment: set `last` to 22 in the body (instead of 0) and re-measure; the prediction is that the surplus grows by roughly the trailer size (up to 9 gate bits plus any radar payload)
if the surplus changes in exactly that way, the trailer is confirmed for this build and the remaining surplus (with last=0) must come from somewhere else
